lines.meet: I'm Ama, and if you get hurt, you tell me straight away. You don't argue when I tell you to sit down, either.
lines.meet_neighbour: I've seen you about Razor Hill. I'm Ama, from the infirmary, and I already know you don't come in when you should.
lines.ask_home: Where are you from, then? Go on, I can never place accents.
lines.ask_work: What did you do before all this, love? You've got the look of somebody who worked shifts.
lines.answer_home: Peckham, south London. I grew up over my dad's phone shop, and I could unlock any phone by the time I was ten.
lines.answer_work: I was a nurse on a children's ward, fourteen years of nights. Four cots to a bay and never enough of us.
lines.chat_food: On nights we lived on toast and whatever the parents brought in. I still can't look at a tin of Quality Street.
lines.chat_sleep: I'm supposed to be in bed by midnight. There's a rule about it in Razor Hill, and everybody knows I break it.
lines.chat_missing: My little brother Kofi used to ring me at four in the morning because he knew I'd be awake. I still wake up at four.
lines.chat_here: Back home there was always a form or a reason you couldn't help somebody. Here there isn't, and that's harder than you'd think.
lines.tease_quiet: {name}, you've said nine words today, and I know because I've been counting. Don't go mad.
lines.tease_talker: {name}, love, I've had toddlers coming round from sedation who talked less than you. I mean that kindly.
lines.tease_careful: {name}, you put your boots on in a set order. I've watched you, and it's the same order every time.
lines.tease_bold: {name}, I've stitched you up twice this week. I'm going to start charging.
lines.tease_any: {name}, you play cards like you're trying to lose. Sit down tonight and I'll take your money properly.
lines.tease_back: That's cheeky, that is. I'll remember it, {name}, and I'll remember it at the card table.
lines.take_it_kindly: Yeah, you've got me there, {name}. Don't let it go to your head.
lines.bristle: Don't start, {name}. I'm not in the mood, and it isn't funny from where I'm standing.
lines.apologise: That was out of order, and I'm sorry. I was tired and I took it out on you.
lines.double_down: No, I meant it. Somebody's got to say it, and it might as well be me.
lines.needle_quiet: If something hurts, you tell me. I can't heal what I don't know about, and you never say a word.
lines.needle_talker: Can you stop talking for five minutes? I'm counting heads and you keep making me lose my place.
lines.needle_careful: We haven't got time for you to check it again. People are hurting while you make your mind up.
lines.needle_bold: You run in, I patch you up, you run in again. I've got other people to look after, you know.
lines.needle_any: You make my job harder than it needs to be, and you don't even notice.
lines.bite_back: Don't you tell me how to do my job. I was doing it before you'd learned to tie your boots.
lines.hurt: Okay, that's me told, then. I'll keep my head down.
lines.laugh_off: Love, I've been shouted at by consultants at four in the morning. You'll have to try harder than that.
lines.confide: {name}, I keep a notebook with every child I lost in it, by first name. I've never told anybody here about it before.
lines.listen: Come here, {name}. That stays with me, and I'm glad you said it.
lines.look_out: {name}, stay where I can see you in there. I can't heal you if you're round a corner.
lines.accept: Fine, {name}, I'll sit down, but only because it's you asking.
lines.deflect: See to the others first, {name}. I'm not the one bleeding.
lines.check_in: {name}, where does it hurt? And don't tell me nowhere, because I'll check anyway.
lines.blame: Somebody broke formation in there, and it wasn't me. I was too busy keeping you all alive.
lines.thank: Thank you for that. I'm usually the one doing the pulling, so it's strange being on the other end.
lines.brush_off: It's my job, love. Now drink some water, and don't argue with me.
lines.worry: {name}, you went grey. Sit down now, and I mean now.
lines.handed_down: Wasn't this yours? I'll give it back if you want it.
lines.hand_fine: You hang on to it, love. It's doing more good on you than it ever did on me.
lines.hand_sulk: Nobody asked me about that. I'll live, but I noticed.
lines.turn_friendly: {name}, you're all right, you are. Come and play cards tonight.
lines.turn_friends: {name}, you're one of my people now. That means I'll shout at you, and I'll always come and find you.
lines.turn_grating: We're not going to get on, are we? Fine, we'll do our jobs and leave it at that.
lines.turn_rivals: I'll heal you, because that's the job. Don't expect me to like it.
lines.make_up: {name}, I've been sharp with you, and you didn't deserve all of it. Come and play cards and we'll call it even.
lines.defend: Leave {name} alone. I was there, and you're blaming the wrong person.
lines.friend_left: I keep looking round for {name} in the fights, and then I remember they've gone home.
lines.friend_back: There you are, {name}. You've lost weight, and I'll be keeping an eye on that.
lines.common_medic: Fourteen years nursing on a children's ward, me. You learn to count heads and beds without even thinking about it.
lines.common_night_work: I did nights for fourteen years. I still feel most awake at four in the morning, and I don't think that'll ever change.
